findings.title: A policy waiver on ANY rule a scan enforces now disables the whole scan, withdrawing enforcement of rules the consumer never exempted
locations: src/Scan.jl:395-399 — apply_ledger, the widened policy loop
src/Scan.jl:390-393 — the docstring paragraph recording the limit
src/Scan.jl:82-112 — rules_register / rules_for_scan, the new resolver
test/scans.jl:172-181 — the testset added with it
findings.before:
id = row["id"]; rule = row["rule"]
    for e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")
        e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)
    end
findings.after:
enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id)))
    for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")
        e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)
    end
findings.why_it_matters: Three catalogued scans are enforced by two rules apiece, and for each the widening hands a waiver on one rule the power to switch the other rule off. Concrete input that used to be refused and now passes: a consumer whose .gbg/exemptions.toml carries `id = "RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE", scope = "policy", target = "*"` (a rule whose check is `["scan:SCAN.DEAD_REF", "panel"]`) and whose docstrings cite a repo path. Before the diff SCAN.DEAD_REF ran, its hard hits were banked as lane 00-scans and `gbg scan docs` was red on RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS; after it, the first target-`*` entry on either enforced rule returns `(Hit[], length(hits), true)` and the whole scan is exempt — the only trace being the note "disabled by the ledger". RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS ("A docstring or error message cites no § number, repo path or inaccessible source") declares SCAN.DEAD_REF as its ONLY check, so nothing else catches it. The same shape holds for SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE, where a RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING waiver now voids RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API, and for SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK in the direction opposite the one the fix was written for (a RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE waiver now also drops the DOI half).
findings.description: The underlying defect — a documented `RULE.CIT.DOI` waiver being silently void because apply_ledger resolved only the catalogue's canonical `rule` column — was real and worth fixing. The edit is wider than that defect: it makes EVERY rule in the scan's `check` closure a kill switch for the whole scan, in both directions, for all three multi-rule scans. The diff's own docstring concedes the consequence ("a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted") and calls it a known limit, but the limit is not pre-existing: before this diff a waiver on the non-canonical rule did nothing at all, so nothing could be withdrawn by it. A narrower repair was available and is not attempted — refusing (or reporting DEAD) when a policy waiver names a rule the scan enforces but cannot attribute, which converts a silent withdrawal of enforcement into a loud one, is the direction the rest of this package takes (`apply_ledger` already throws LedgerError when a text scan meets an `arg_type` predicate it cannot evaluate). The oracle does not cover the new direction: the added testset asserts the DOI case, the canonical case, and that `RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS` waives nothing — but RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS is unrelated to SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK, so the assertion that an unrelated rule waives nothing says nothing about the sibling-withdrawal case, and neither SCAN.DEAD_REF nor SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE is exercised at all.
findings.evidence: policy/RULES.toml: RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE `check = ["scan:SCAN.DEAD_REF", "panel"]`, RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS `check = ["scan:SCAN.DEAD_REF"]`, RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING `check = ["scan:SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE", …]`, RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API `check = ["scan:SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE"]`; catalog/scans.toml: `id = "SCAN.DEAD_REF" / rule = "RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS"`, `id = "SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE" / rule = "RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API"`; src/Scan.jl:390-393 "The mirror case is NOT fixed and is a known limit: a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan"; test/scans.jl:181 `@test !isempty(G.run_scan(d, row; ledger = pol("RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS")).hits) # an unrelated rule waives nothing`

findings.title: close's new build-staleness branch fails open: any git failure, and the `0`×40 head build records itself, make it pass vacuously
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:323 — the head the record is written with
src/CLI/Passes.jl:1241 — the sibling guard the comment cites
test/rounds.jl:546, 659, 723, 1018-1025 — the four records re-baselined to satisfy it
findings.before: isempty(dirty) || push!(fails, "the round's files are not committed: " …)\n    st = Preflight.stamps(cfg; record = rec)   # no build was consulted at all
findings.after: moved = Git.changed_paths(root, "$(b["head"])..HEAD", Preflight.covered_paths(cfg))\n            isempty(moved) || push!(fails, "the recorded docs build is stale — " …)
findings.why_it_matters: Git.changed_paths is `String.(filter(!isempty, split(something(run(root, "diff", "--name-only", range, "--", paths...), ""), '\n')))`, and Git.run returns `nothing` on ANY non-zero exit. So when the recorded head is unreachable — a squashed or amended fix pass, a round whose build ran in a checkout since rewritten, or `Rounds.build`'s own `something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40)` sentinel written when git was absent — `git diff <head>..HEAD` fails, `moved` is empty, and the staleness branch reports a green current build for a build that may predate every fix in the round. The third of the three conditions this guard exists for is therefore the one that silently does not hold, and the failure is silent by construction: the reader sees close accept, not a skipped check.
findings.description: The guard itself is warranted — 2026-09-12-check-docs-01 graded two passes over a red build — and the missing/red branches are sound. The staleness branch is not. Its comment claims "The staleness test is the one `audit_after_code` uses", but the test it actually copies from lives 70 lines below in the same function (the audit-changes branch, Passes.jl:1241) and is a PAIR: `Git.run(root, "cat-file", "-e", a["head"] * "^{commit}") === nothing ? push!(fails, "staleness UNCHECKABLE: the audited head … is unreachable") : (isempty(stale) || push!(fails, …))`. The reachability half — the half that converts an unanswerable question into a refusal rather than a pass — is dropped. Nothing else compensates: `Rounds.build` writes `"0"^40` rather than refusing when `Git.head` returns nothing, and round.schema.json's `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` pattern accepts that sentinel, so a record that is structurally valid can be semantically unanswerable. The oracle is on the wrong side of this too: the three new close branches have no test at all (no test/ file mentions "no docs build is recorded", "the recorded docs build" or the stale message), while four pre-existing round records were edited in the same diff to carry `"build" => Dict("code" => 0, "head" => …)` and the round-lifecycle testset now writes that record by hand rather than calling `Rounds.build` — the guard is satisfied everywhere it is met and asserted nowhere.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Git.jl: `changed_paths(root, range, paths) = String.(filter(!isempty, split(something(run(root, "diff", "--name-only", range, "--", paths...), ""), '\n')))` and `run` … `catch; return nothing`; src/CLI/Rounds.jl:323 `rec["build"] = Dict{String,Any}("code" => code, "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40), "at" => timestamp())`; src/CLI/Passes.jl:1158 "The staleness test is the one `audit_after_code` uses" vs :1241 "staleness UNCHECKABLE: the audited head $(first(a["head"], 8)) is unreachable"; test/rounds.jl:546 `"build" => Dict{String,Any}("code" => 0, "head" => something(G.Git.head(root), "0"^40), "at" => "2026-01-01T00:00:03")`

findings.title: The panel's authored-source grant is REPLACED by latex_source_globs, so a consumer that set that key loses ext/, docs/src/ and docs/ from five hats' reading surface
locations: test/coverage.jl:106-121 — the testset added with it
findings.before: if (needs.includes('source')) parts.push(`ALSO the AUTHORED SOURCE (read it with Read/Grep; quote findings at file:line): the docstrings under ${A.repo}/src/ and ${A.repo}/ext/, the pages under ${A.repo}/docs/src/, and the rationale documents under ${A.repo}/docs/.`)
findings.why_it_matters: The fallback fires only when the key is EMPTY, so any consumer that has set it — ARCHITECTURE documents `latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]` as the worked example (§ line 1241) and `latex_source_globs = ["src/*.jl"]` as one consumer's actual value (line 1353) — now has the five `needs: source` hats told their authored source is that list and nothing else. Under `["src/*.jl"]` the invariants-and-decisions hat is no longer pointed at `docs/` (the rationale and decision documents it exists to audit), doc-policy and naming-policy lose `ext/` docstrings and `docs/src/` pages, and latex-typesetter loses every page whose markup it is the only hat asked to read. The hats keep their instruction to quote findings at their source file:line, so a defect outside the globs is not merely unreported — it is unquotable. This reduces what the panel can reject, on exactly the consumers that configured the key.
findings.description: Two defects were being fixed: panel.js carrying package paths as literals (a core-invariant breach) and latex_source_globs having no reader. Both are real. The edit is wider than either: it does not give the key a reader, it makes the key the DEFINITION of a different and larger surface. The key's own name, its schema entry (`$ref: strlist`, `default: []`, no description) and its ARCHITECTURE examples all describe LaTeX source globs for the typesetting hat; nothing in the config's documented contract says setting it narrows what every source hat may read. The stated motivation — "a consumer naming examples/*.jl had its Literate surface silently never read" — is served by a UNION with the four default surfaces, which adds the missing surface without removing three; replacement is the only variant that can subtract. The change is invisible to the consumer: no verb reports which globs a hat received, and the fallback hides it from the tool itself, whose own config sets `latex_source_globs = []` (ARCHITECTURE line 1418), so the tool as its own fifth consumer exercises only the default branch. The new coverage test asserts that panel.js reads `A.source_globs` and that preflight emits a non-empty value — over `fixture_config()`, which is likewise the empty-key branch — so the narrowing direction is asserted nowhere.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1241 `latex_source_globs   = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]`; :1353 "`design_docs_withheld = [\"architecture\"]`, `latex_source_globs = [\"src/*.jl\"]`"; :1418 `latex_source_globs = []` (the tool's own); schema/config.schema.json:441-444 `"latex_source_globs": {"$ref": "#/$defs/strlist", "default": []}`; catalog/hats/invariants-and-decisions.toml:4 `needs = ["rulebook", "source"]`, catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml:10 "Quote the rule and the violation, the violation at its source file:line"; test/coverage.jl:118-121 asserts only `!isempty(a["source_globs"])`

findings.title: gbg release now admits every open docs round to its own SELF.DOCS build, suppressing the gate's per-round refusals including :committed
locations: test/gate.jl:41-74 — the testset added with it
findings.after: admitted = admitted_rounds(cfg)\n        … ("docs build (SELF.DOCS)", addenv(`… docs/make.jl`, "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP" => "1", "GBG_ROUND" => admitted))
findings.why_it_matters: GBG_ROUND is consumed in gate_problems as `r.name in ignored && continue`, and the `continue` sits ABOVE the `:committed` check as well as producing the `:open` skip — so admitting a round suppresses both refusals for it, not one. Input that was refused and is now accepted: `gbg release 1.0.0-rc.10` while `2026-09-12-check-docs-01` is open. Before, the release's own docs build hit the gate, exited 1 with GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP set, and the release refused with "docs build (SELF.DOCS) failed"; now the gate passes that round over and the release proceeds to tag and push. The claim that this "restores the permission without weakening the guarantee" holds only for the guarantee it names (a build that did not happen still cannot pass, since GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP is unchanged); the freeze that `gate` itself enforces — a docs build during an open round runs only through `gbg round build <round>`, so the round's artefacts and the built site stay in step — is genuinely lifted for the release path.
findings.description: The dead-branch diagnosis is correct and the intent is defensible: `if !rc` was written to let a candidate be cut mid-round and could never be exercised. But the admission is unconditional and unscoped — it is computed for a final release too (harmless only because release_fails refuses on any open round first), and it admits open rounds of BOTH docs instruments regardless of which one, if any, the release relates to. The narrower edit that matches the stated intent is to admit rounds only on the rc path, and only for the reason given. The `:committed` leak is largely covered in practice, because release_fails' `isempty(Git.porcelain(root))` refuses an unclean tree before the build runs and an untracked or modified round directory makes it unclean; that is why this is minor rather than major. It is reported because the weakening is not the one the comment describes: the comment says the build is admitted, the code says the round is excused from every per-round refusal the gate makes.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Gate.jl:85-92 `r.name in ignored && continue` immediately preceding both the `:open` push and the `!in_ci … :committed` push; src/CLI/Release.jl:70 `admitted_rounds(cfg::AbstractDict) = join(frozen_rounds(cfg, Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS...), ",")` — no `rc` argument; src/CLI/Release.jl:165 "a release still never accepts a build that did not happen, it only stops refusing one that can"

findings.title: release gained a `root` keyword while `running_dev()` still tests the RUNNING copy, so the guard no longer names the checkout that gets tagged and pushed
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:148-156 — the new signature and the unchanged guard
src/CLI/Release.jl:178-179 — the tag and push, now over `root`
docs/prose_shape.csv:44 — the documented signature, re-measured 178 → 242 words
findings.before:
function release(ver::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout, skip_tests::Bool = false)
    …
    root = pkgdir(GBGCodingTools)
    running_dev() || (println(io, "release: the dev checkout only"); return 2)
findings.after:
function release(ver::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout, skip_tests::Bool = false,
                 root::AbstractString = pkgdir(GBGCodingTools))
    …
    running_dev() || (println(io, "release: the dev checkout only"); return 2)
    cfg = Config.read(root)
findings.why_it_matters: `running_dev() = get(ENV, "GBG_DEV", "") == "1" || ispath(joinpath(pkgdir(GBGCodingTools), ".git"))` answers a question about the running package only. Before the diff that was also the repository being tagged, by construction. Now `release("1.2.3"; root = "/some/other/checkout")` passes the guard on the tool's own `.git` and then runs `Git.run(root, "tag", "-a", "v1.2.3", …)` and `Git.run(root, "push", "origin", "v1.2.3")` against a repository the guard never inspected — with every refusal (branch, changelog, Project.toml version, rounds) read from that other root, and the carry ledger written there. The refusal message "release: the dev checkout only" now states something the code no longer checks.
findings.description: The motive — the verb was untestable and its rc branch had never run — is sound, and lifting `release_fails` out was the right half of the change. The `root` keyword is the half that widens a public, documented binding (it carries a docstring and appears in the prose-shape register) in order to reach a test, and it decouples the one guard the verb has from the object the verb acts on. Two narrower shapes were available and are not taken: give only `release_fails` the `root` (which is what all the new tests but one actually exercise — `release_fails(cfg, root, …)` is called directly in the second testset), or re-derive the guard from the argument (`ispath(joinpath(root, ".git"))`), so that the thing checked and the thing tagged stay the same object. The docstring's own defence, "the CLI never passes it", is a statement about one caller, not a guard.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Main.jl:76 `running_dev() = get(ENV, "GBG_DEV", "") == "1" || ispath(joinpath(pkgdir(GBGCodingTools), ".git"))`; src/CLI/Release.jl:178-179 `Git.run(root, "tag", "-a", "v$ver", …)`, `Git.run(root, "push", "origin", "v$ver")`; src/CLI/Release.jl:143 "the CLI never passes it"; test/rounds.jl (release_fails testset) `clean(rc) = G.release_fails(cfg, root, rc ? "0.1.0-rc.1" : "0.1.0", "0.1.0", rc)`
